summary: N3 shared helper code: five support helpers in util.c are called by fourteen unrelated parsers in three other files. v2 adds an overflow check to the most widely shared helper (ut_parse_u32); v3 rewrites it cosmetically, fixes another shared helper (ut_eq_nocase) and gives one unrelated caller its own change. Callers never change textually just because a helper does.

pairs.intent: A helper shared by twelve unrelated callers across three parsers gains an overflow check. None of the callers changes textually, yet all of them behave differently on overflowing input. A matcher that propagates change along call edges, or that compares callers by what they call, flags eleven or twelve unchanged functions; the callers share nothing with each other except the callee.

pairs.intent: Three independent edits in one step: the shared parser is only rewritten cosmetically (locals renamed, identical machine code), the shared case-folding comparison is fixed, and one unrelated caller gets its own error-handling change. The other callers of the two touched helpers stay text-identical, so the one real caller change has to be told apart from twelve look-alike callers that merely sit on changed code.
